title: Concurrent Closing Conditions
subject: Contracts
stem: The former lumberyard parcel included a small office, a fenced materials pad, and a metal storage shed. Caleb agreed to buy it from Mary. The contract named a closing date but did not say that either side had to perform before the other. At the title company on the closing date, Caleb said he would release the purchase money only after Mary handed over the signed deed. Mary said she would hand over the signed deed only after Caleb released the money. Neither tendered first, and Mary sued Caleb for breach. Who is most likely to prevail?

choices.A: Neither on this record, because payment and deed delivery at a land closing are concurrent conditions, and each party generally must be ready and able to tender performance.
choices.B: Caleb, because a seller must always deliver the deed before the buyer has any duty to appear with the purchase price.
choices.C: Mary, because Caleb's statement that he would not release funds first was an anticipatory repudiation.
choices.D: Mary, because a buyer must always pay the price before the seller tenders a deed.

rightExplanation: Neither party is likely to prevail on this record. When a land-sale contract sets a closing but does not specify the order of performance, the buyer's payment and the seller's delivery of the deed are concurrent conditions. Each party must tender, or be ready and able to tender, its own performance. Caleb did not have to pay first, and Mary did not have to deliver the deed first. Because both refused to tender except after the other performed, Mary cannot establish Caleb's breach.

wrongExplanations.B: The seller-first sequence is attractive because deed delivery is the seller's central duty. The breaker is that simultaneous closing duties are concurrent conditions, so the seller has no unconditional duty to perform first.
wrongExplanations.C: Caleb's refusal to release funds first sounds like a repudiation. The breaker is that insisting on concurrent tender is not an unequivocal refusal to perform the contract.
wrongExplanations.D: The buyer-first sequence is attractive because payment is the buyer's main performance. The breaker is that a land closing normally requires simultaneous tender when the contract does not assign first performance.
